The second was your third-year class standing, where you are in the lowest decile; accepted students average around the sixth decile. Your high family income was the third most influential factor and was the only top signal pushing the other way, toward passing, but it was not enough to offset the academic concerns. Your undergraduate GPA of 3.30 is roughly in line with accepted students, so it did not explain the denial. Because the model’s main concern is bar readiness, you should focus next on strengthening the areas most associated with failure. Consider intensive LSAT preparation and retaking the exam, seek academic advising or bar-readiness support, and ask admissions how to document improvement before reapplying. A later application with a stronger test score and clear evidence of academic progress would better address the model’s concerns.
